sentences.text:
Proceedings in the present case arises from filing of DAR by the investigating officer in FIR No.
1280/21 PS Nihal Vihar, regarding the accident in question.

As per the documents annexed with the DAR, on 11.11.2021 at about 8.30 to 8.45 PM at Main Najafgarh-Nangloi Road, near Salasar Garden,
Nihal Vihar, Delhi, a motorcycle bearing Temporary no. DL04TC0515 (Registration No.
DL4SDK8758 subsequently assigned) (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 1, in fast speed and in rash and negligent manner, hit the padestrian (petitioner) and due to the forceful impact of hitting, petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

It is further stated that the petitioner / injured was rushed to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Mangol Puri, Delhi,
wherein he was medically examined vide MLC no. 24731 dated 11.11.2021.
2.
IO filed the DAR giving details of respondent no.1 being the driver as well as owner of the offending vehicle and the respondent no. 2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle.

DAR was also accompanied with other relevant documents including final report U/s 173 Cr.PC, MLC of injured,
mechanical inspection report of the vehicle, seizure memo of the vehicle, its documents, site plan,
notice U/s 133 M.V. Act and its reply etc.
3.

A reply/written statement has been filed on behalf of the respondent no.1, wherein it is stated inter alia that the police has falsely implicated the driver/ owner of the vehicle bearing no.
DL4SDK8758 in the present FIR; that the accident in question was not occurred due to the negligence of the driver of bike in question; that the accident had occurred due to negligence of the SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 16:19:20 +0530 Date: 2024.09.12 MACT No.
1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 petitioner, who was crossing the road in a drunken condition and without obeying the traffic rules; that the FIR was registered against the driver at the instance and connivance of the petitioner; that the vehicle in vehicle was insured with Cholamandalam MS Insurance Company Limited vide policy cum certificate no. 3397/03096629/000/00 for the period from 11.11.2021 to 10.11.2026; that there is no breach in terms and conditions of the policy,
therefore, driver/owner shall have no liability to compensate the petitioner and Insurance Co. shall have liability to compensate the petitioner.

It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand &

sentences.text: The onus to prove this issue was placed on the petitioner.
Petitioner/PW-1 tendered his affidavit in evidence which is Ex.PW1/A.

He has relied upon the documents i.e. (i) Copy of Final Report Ex.PW1/1; (ii) Copy of MLC Ex.PW1/2;
(iii) Copy of DAR Ex.PW1/3; (iv) Copy of Aadhar Card Ex.PW1/4 (OSR); (v) Copy of disability certificate Ex.PW1/5 (OSR); (vi) Medical prescription Ex.PW1/6 (Colly) and (vii) Copy of medical bills Ex.PW1/7 (Colly).

In his cross- examination done by the Ld. counsel for the respondent no. 1,
PW-1 stated inter alia that the accident took place on 11.11.2021; that he does not know when the accident took place as he was fainted on the spot; that he was accompanied alongwith his wife on the date of accident but his wife was far away when the SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.09.12 16:19:42 +0530 MACT No. 1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 accident took place; that he was walking on the side of the road when the accident took place and he did not see the person who hit him as he got fainted.

He denied that Vikas has been implicated wrongly in the present case or that accident did not take place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 or that the accident took place while he was crossing the road in the drunken state or that he was not obeying traffic rule or that he was deposing falsely.
11. PW-1 deposed in lines with the petition and has well explained the mode and manner of the accident.

From the careful perusal of the testimony of the injured / PW-1 including his cross examination, there is nothing material has been elicited which would cast doubt over his credibility and trustworthiness, to disbelieve the version of accident as given by PW-1.

Moreover, the factum of accident has not even been disputed by the respondent no. 1, however, he has taken the plea that accident was not caused due to his negligence but it was caused due to the negligence of petitioner,
who was drunk and negligently crossing the road in drunken state.
However, he has failed to lead any cogent evidence in support of his plea.
Whereas, it is evident from the testimony of PW-1 that respondent could not impeach his testimony through litmus test of cross-examination.
PW-1 himself is the injured having sustained injuries due to the accident in question.
There is no reason as to why he would depose falsely against the respondent no.1.
The testimony of PW- 1 remained unimpeachable on the aspect of accident in question.
There is no possibility of false implication of respondent and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioner herein.

Act by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.

Petitioner in his evidence has also placed reliance on the DAR,
which include the report u/s 173 Cr.PC filed by IO in FIR No. 1280/21 PS Nihal Vihar, site plan of the accident, MLC of injured, seizure memo of vehicle, its documents, mechanical inspection report Jugal Mahto vs Vikas And Ors on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198499977/

13. Respondent no. 1 got himself examined and deposed on the lines of his reply filed in the present matter.

He also deposed that at the time of accident, he was having a properly verified authentic license to drive which was granted by the Transport Department, Delhi, which is a Learner's license and valid from 25.08.2021 to 24.02.2022.
His affidavit in evidence Ex.RW1/A.

He has relied upon the documents i.e. (i) vehicle particulars Ex.RW1/1; (ii) Insurance Policy Ex.RW1/2 and (iii)
Learner's license Ex.RW1/3.
In his cross examination done by the Ld. Counsel for the respondent no.2, he admitted that at the time of accident, he had learning license.
He denied that due to breach of terms and conditions of the insurance policy, the insurance company holds no liability to compensate the claimant.

In his cross examination done by the Ld. Counsel for the petitioner, he admitted that he was driving the offending vehicle SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 16:20:05 +0530 Date: 2024.09.12 MACT No. 1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 at the time of accident and his wife Vishaka was the pillion rider.
He also admitted that the vehicle bearing no. DL4SDK8758 was insured vide policy valid from 11.11.2021 to 10.11.2026 at the time of accident.
He denied that the accident was caused due to his negligence.
He stated that he has not filed any document to show that the claimant was in drunken state.
He denied that petitioner was obeying the traffic rules at the time of accident.
He denied that the accident occurred due to his rash and negligence.
He admitted that his vehicle bearing no. DL4SDK8758 was involved in the accident.
14. The factum of accident as well as driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 have been duly admitted by the respondent no. 1.

Although, he has taken the plea that accident in question was not occurred due to his negligence but it was occurred due to the negligence of petitioner, who was drunk and negligently crossing the road in drunken state.
However, the said plea is not substantiated by any cogent evidence brought on record on behalf of respondent no. 1.
Even the MLC of the injured does not reflect that injured was under the influence of alcohol at that time.

Rather, the evidence of petitioner (PW-1) which is corroborated by the various documents filed alongwith the DAR, clearly shows that accident in question was caused by the respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle in rash and negligent manner.

Hence, the evidence of respondent does not offer him any help to absolve him of his involvement in the present matter much less to discard the incriminating material available against him in the present case.

15. Furthermore, in the given facts and circumstances of SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 16:20:11 +0530 Date: 2024.09.12 MACT No. 1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 the present case, the rashness and negligence of the driver (R1) would also be assumed by virtue of res ipsa loquitur.

The very factum that the driver of offending vehicle (respondent no. 1) had hit it against the pedestrian also shows that he was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently, which became out of his control and he could not apply its brakes at the right time and caused the accident in question.
There was an implicit duty on the respondent no.1 to see that his driving did not endanger the life of any other user of the road.
He has failed to exercise the caution incumbent upon him and has clearly neglected his duty of circumspection.

sentences.text: Thus, in view of the aforesaid discussion and the evidence which has come on record, it is held that the petitioner has been able to prove on the basis of preponderance of probabilities that he had sustained injuries in road accident which took place on 11.11.2021 at about 8.30 to 8.45 PM at Main Najafgarh-Nangloi Road, near Salasar Garden, Nihal Vihar, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by respondent no. 1.
Accordingly, issue no.1 stands decided in favour of petitioner.
ISSUE No.2 17.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.

Section 168 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 enjoins upon the claim Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation, which appears to be just and reasonable.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.

A man is not compensated for SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 16:20:18 +0530 Date: 2024.09.12 MACT No.
1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 the physical injury, he is compensated for the loss which he suffers as a result of that injury (Baker v. Willoughby (1970) Ac 467 at page 492 per Lord Reid).
COMPUTATION OF COMPENSATION 18.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned,
they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort, disappointment, hardship, frustration SACHIN

Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.09.12 16:20:25 +0530 MACT No. 1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 and mental stress in life."
19.
Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

sentences.text: The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:

Pecuniary Damages (special damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.09.12 16:20:33 +0530 MACT No.
1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
 Non-Pecuniary Damages (general  damages)
 (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

sentences.text: In routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b),
(iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
20.

In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-

Medical Expenses:
21. PW-1 i.e. the injured himself, has inter alia deposed in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A that he also took private treatment and he is still under treatment and incurred more than Rs.7,00,000/- on treatment, medicines, conveyances and special diet.
He has filed on record copy of his MLC Ex.PW1/2, Medical Prescription Ex.PW1/6 (Colly) and Medical bills Ex.PW1/7 (Colly).
In his cross examination done by the Ld. Counsel for the respondent no.2, he admitted that bills placed by him are not properly stamped bearing GST number indicating hospital name or pharmacy shop.
He denied that medical bills are false and fabricated.
He denied that he has not incurred amount of Rs. 7 lacs on his treatment, medicines, conveyance and special diet.
He denied that he has not suffered any loss or capacity to earn.
He admitted that he has not placed any documentary proof to show the mode of payment of the expenses incurred for his medical treatment.
He denied that he had not made any payment or incurred any expenses with respect to his medical treatment and bills.
He also denied that medical bills had been issued in the name of some other person and the same does not bear his name.

22. The petitioner has placed on record certain documents, which are collectively Ex.PW1/7, which are stated to be medical bills, however, perusal of the same shows that most of them are 'Rough Estimates', some receipt vouchers are unsigned, unstamped without Doctor's prescription and some invoices are in the name of other persons.
Hence, petitioner has failed to prove on record the medical bills in support of his contentions for incurring expenses on his treatment, medicines etc.

Ld. Counsel for the respondent / Insurance Co. has argued that petitioner was SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 16:20:46 +0530 Date: 2024.09.12 MACT No. 1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 admitted in government hospital i.e. Sanjay Gandhi Memorial Hospital,
Mangolpuri, Delhi and did not spent any amount on his treatment
and therefore, he is not entitled for any compensation under this head.

Although, petitioner has not been able to prove the medical bills or any other expenditure allegedly incurred by him on account of his medical treatment,
however, at the same time, it cannot be overlooked that petitioner, who has sustained grievous injuries in the accident, would have definitely spent some amount on medicines which were not available in the hospital at that time or the medicines which he would have required post discharge from the hospital.

Thus, even in the absence of any bills for his medical treatment, in view of the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner as well as surrounding circumstances, I find it Jugal Mahto vs Vikas And Ors on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198499977/
8 appropriate to award a sum of Rs. 20,000/- as notional amount to him on account of medical expenses under this head.
Loss of income during treatment period 23. PW-1 has deposed inter alia in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A that he was doing the work of 'Mistry' and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and due to said accident, he lost his earning and suffered a lot of monetary loss apart from suffering from mental pain and agony.

sentences.text: In his cross examination, he denied that he was not earning Rs.20,000/- per month at the time of accident and that is why, he had not placed any document regarding the same.

Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 2 /
Insurance Co. has vehemently argued that petitioner is resident of Bihar, which is very much reflected from the Aadhar Card filed by him on record and he has not placed on record any document to show that he was residing or working in Delhi and earning a sum of SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.09.12 16:20:52 +0530 MACT No. 1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 Rs.20,000/- as alleged.
It is evident from the record that there is no document placed on record by the petitioner to show that he was residing or working in Delhi.
There is no other witness got examined by him in support of his vocation and monthly income as alleged.
As per the Aadhar Card filed by him, he is a resident of Bihar.

Thus, for want of cogent and definite evidence being led by petitioner with regard to his vocation and actual monthly income, this Tribunal assesses the income of the injured to be at parity with minimum wages of Unskilled person in the State of Bihar which at the time of accident i.e. 11.11.2021 was Rs.280/- per day.
Hence, the monthly income of the petitioner for the purpose of computation of compensation in the present case is assessed as Rs. 8,400/- (Rs.280/- X 30 days).

24. Petitioner has deposed that after the accident, he was taken to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital,
Mangolpuri, Delhi, wherein he was medically examined vide MLC No. 24371; that he also took private treatment; that due to this accident, he became incapacitated and since this accident, he has not been in a position to earn and he had to sell his agricultural property at his native village for his treatment and livelihood.

In his cross examination, he admitted that he had not filed any document to show that he was not able to earn and he had to sell his agricultural property at his native village for his treatment and livelihood of his family.
He denied that he had not suffered any loss or capacity to earn or any loss due to the said accident.
Admittedly, there is no document placed on record by the petitioner to show that he had to sell his agricultural land for the purpose of his medical treatment.

However, considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2024.09.12 16:20:59 +0530 MACT No. 1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 material placed on record as well as surrounding circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that injured/petitioner would have not been able to work for a period of about 06 months.
Accordingly, this Tribunal hereby grant compensation of sum of Rs. 50,400/- (Rs. 8,400/- x 6) to the petitioner under this head towards loss of income during treatment period.

Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 2 /

Although, there is no document placed on record by him to substantiate his plea for incurring expenses on account of special diet, conveyance and attendance, at the same time, it cannot be overlooked that he had sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

Thus, he would have taken special rich protein diet for his speedy recovery and would have also incurred some amount towards conveyance charges while commuting to the concerned hospital as OPD patient for his regular checkup and follow up during the period of his medical treatment.

He would also have been definitely helped by some person either outsider or from his family, to perform his daily activities as also while visiting the hospital during the course of his medical treatment.

In the absence of any such documentary proof, this Tribunal while taking into consideration the nature of injuries suffered by him as well as surrounding circumstances, finds it appropriate to grant notional amount i.e. a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards conveyance charges, a sum of SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 16:21:05 +0530 Date: 2024.09.12 MACT No. 1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 Rs.30,000/- towards special diet and a sum of Rs.50,000/-

opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the injured Jugul Mahto suffered injuries in a vehicular accident that took place on 11.11.2021 at about 8.30 to 8.45 pm at Main Najafgarh- Nangloi Road, Near Salasar Garden, Nihal Vihar, Delhi involving a vehicle no. DL4SDK8758 (offending vehicle) being driven and owned by respondent no.1/Vikas in a rash and negligent manner and insured with respondent no.2 Cholamandlam MS General Insurance Company Limited?
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
However, he has failed to lead any cogent evidence in support of his plea.
The testimony of PW- 1 remained unimpeachable on the aspect of accident in question.
There is no possibility of false implication of respondent and/or false involvement of offending vehicle at the instance of petitioner herein.
Furthermore, the respondent no. 1 namely Vikas (accused in State case) has been charge-sheeted (which is part of copies of criminal case available on record) for offences punishable U/s 279/338 IPC and 3/181 M.V. Act by the investigating agency after arriving at the conclusion on the basis of investigation carried out by it that the accident in question had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by him.
However, the said plea is not substantiated by any cogent evidence brought on record on behalf of respondent no. 1.
Even the MLC of the injured does not reflect that injured was under the influence of alcohol at that time.
Rather, the evidence of petitioner (PW-1) which is corroborated by the various documents filed alongwith the DAR, clearly shows that accident in question was caused by the respondent no. 1 while driving the offending vehicle in rash and negligent manner.
Hence, the evidence of respondent does not offer him any help to absolve him of his involvement in the present matter much less to discard the incriminating material available against him in the present case.
The very factum that the driver of offending vehicle (respondent no. 1) had hit it against the pedestrian also shows that he was driving the vehicle rashly and negligently, which became out of his control and he could not apply its brakes at the right time and caused the accident in question.
There was an implicit duty on the respondent no.1 to see that his driving did not endanger the life of any other user of the road.
In view of the finding on issue no.1, petitioner is entitled to get compensation, however, the quantum of compensation still needs to be adjudicated.
As per settled law, compensation is not expected to be windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b),
(iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life.
20.
Thus, even in the absence of any bills for his medical treatment, in view of the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner as well as surrounding circumstances, I find it Jugal Mahto vs Vikas And Ors on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198499977/
8 appropriate to award a sum of Rs. 20,000/- as notional amount to him on account of medical expenses under this head.
Loss of income during treatment period 23. PW-1 has deposed inter alia in his evidence by way of affidavit Ex.PW1/A that he was doing the work of 'Mistry' and earning Rs.20,000/- per month and due to said accident, he lost his earning and suffered a lot of monetary loss apart from suffering from mental pain and agony.
In the absence of any such documentary proof, this Tribunal while taking into consideration the nature of injuries suffered by him as well as surrounding circumstances, finds it appropriate to grant notional amount i.e. a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards conveyance charges, a sum of SACHIN Digitally signed by SACHIN GUPTA GUPTA 16:21:05 +0530 Date: 2024.09.12 MACT No. 1155/22 Date of Award: 12.09.2024 Rs.30,000/- towards special diet and a sum of Rs.50,000/-
towards attendant charges to the petitioner.
Insurance Company has sought to avoid its liability to pay the compensation amount on the ground that there was fundamental breach of the terms and conditions of insurance policy on the part of insured as respondent no. 1 (driver of the offending vehicle) was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and he was possessing only a Learner's Driving License and no other person was sitting with him as a pillion rider holding a valid driving license as per the provisions of M.V. Act, for that reasons, he has been chargesheet u/s 3/181 M.V. Act
Further, the motorcycle was not having any signage of 'L' as per the requirement of learning DL and M.V. Act and, therefore, Insurance Co. is not liable to pay any amount of compensation to the petitioner and in such an eventuality, the owner/driver of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation amount.
However, respondent no. 1 has failed to establish on record that at the Jugal Mahto vs Vikas And Ors on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198499977/
12 time, when he was driving the offending vehicle, he was accompanied by a person duly licensed to drive the vehicle and that he was in compliance of the aforesaid provision of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 in this regard.
In view of the aforesaid, it is clear that there is violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy on the part of insured.
Thus, insurance company is entitled to recovery rights against the respondent no. 1 Sh. Vikas.
